# chrome-dev-control

Bash-invokable Chrome DevTools scripts for AI agents. Navigate, screenshot, click, inspect - no MCP setup needed.

16 CLI tools for page management, DOM interaction, screenshots, console/network inspection, and performance tracing.

## CRITICAL FOR AI AGENTS

These are custom CLI wrappers - NOT standard npm packages. Never use Playwright, Puppeteer, or Selenium.

```bash
# CORRECT - invoke directly
chrome-navigate.js "http://localhost:3000"
chrome-snapshot.js

# WRONG - don't do these
node chrome-navigate.js          # No 'node' prefix
npx playwright test              # NEVER use Playwright
npm install puppeteer            # NEVER install browser libs
```

## Setup

1. Clone/download to your preferred location
2. Install dependencies:
```bash
cd ~/agent-tools/chrome-dev-control
npm install
```

3. Add to PATH in `~/.zshrc` or `~/.bashrc`:
```bash
export PATH="$HOME/agent-tools/chrome-dev-control:$PATH"
```

4. Reload shell:
```bash
source ~/.zshrc
```

5. Verify:
```bash
chrome-navigate.js --help
```

Prerequisites:
- Chrome browser running with DevTools accessible
- Node.js 18+

## How to Invoke These Tools

**CRITICAL FOR AGENTS**: These are executable scripts in your PATH. When invoking via the Bash tool:

CORRECT:
```bash
chrome-snapshot.js
chrome-click.js "submit-btn"
chrome-navigate.js "https://example.com"
```

INCORRECT:
```bash
node chrome-snapshot.js          # Don't use 'node' prefix
./chrome-snapshot.js             # Don't use './' prefix
```

## Snapshot (Most Important)

```bash
chrome-snapshot.js
chrome-snapshot.js --verbose
chrome-snapshot.js --file /tmp/snapshot.txt
```

Take an accessibility tree snapshot. Returns element UIDs needed for all interactions.

**Always run this first.** UIDs from the snapshot are required for click, fill, drag, etc.

**Options:**
- `--verbose`: Include full a11y tree details
- `--file PATH`: Save to file instead of stdout

## Screenshot

```bash
chrome-screenshot.js --file /tmp/page.png
chrome-screenshot.js --full --file /tmp/full.png
chrome-screenshot.js --uid "hero-image" --file /tmp/element.png
chrome-screenshot.js --format jpeg --quality 85 --file /tmp/page.jpg
```

Capture viewport, full page, or specific element.

**Options:**
- `--full`: Full scrollable page (not just viewport)
- `--uid ID`: Capture specific element by UID
- `--file PATH`: Save to file (required)
- `--format FMT`: png, jpeg, webp (default: png)
- `--quality N`: 0-100 for jpeg/webp

**Screenshot Size Limits:**
Claude API has an 8000px max image dimension. For long pages, use `chrome-split-image.js` to split into viewable sections.

**Workflow for full-page screenshots:**
```bash
# 1. Take full-page screenshot
chrome-screenshot.js --full --file /tmp/full-page.png

# 2. Check dimensions / split if needed
chrome-split-image.js /tmp/full-page.png

# 3. View each section (output will list created files)
# Files: /tmp/full-page-1.png, /tmp/full-page-2.png, etc.
```

## Click

```bash
chrome-click.js "submit-btn"
chrome-click.js "folder-icon" --double
chrome-click.js "dropdown-menu" --hover
```

Click, double-click, or hover on elements.

**Options:**
- `--double`: Double-click
- `--hover`: Hover only (no click)

## Fill

```bash
chrome-fill.js "email-input" "user@example.com"
chrome-fill.js "country-select" "United States"
chrome-fill.js --form '[{"uid":"email","value":"a@b.com"},{"uid":"pass","value":"secret"}]'
```

Fill inputs, textareas, or select dropdowns.

**Options:**
- `--form JSON`: Fill multiple fields at once

## Keys

```bash
chrome-keys.js "Enter"
chrome-keys.js "Escape"
chrome-keys.js "Control+A"
chrome-keys.js "Control+Shift+R"
chrome-keys.js "ArrowDown"
```

Press keyboard keys or combinations.

Modifiers: `Control`, `Shift`, `Alt`, `Meta`

## Scroll

```bash
chrome-scroll.js down
chrome-scroll.js down 1000
chrome-scroll.js up 300
chrome-scroll.js top
chrome-scroll.js bottom
chrome-scroll.js page-down
chrome-scroll.js page-up
chrome-scroll.js --to "footer"
chrome-scroll.js --to "section-3" --instant
```

Scroll the page or to a specific element.

**Directions:**
- `down [px]`: Scroll down (default: 500px)
- `up [px]`: Scroll up (default: 500px)
- `top`: Jump to top of page
- `bottom`: Jump to bottom of page
- `page-down`: Scroll one viewport height down
- `page-up`: Scroll one viewport height up

**Element Scrolling:**
- `--to <uid>`: Scroll element into view (smooth)
- `--to <uid> --instant`: Scroll element into view (instant)

## Navigate

```bash
chrome-navigate.js "https://example.com"
chrome-navigate.js --back
chrome-navigate.js --forward
chrome-navigate.js --reload
chrome-navigate.js --reload --no-cache
chrome-navigate.js --new "https://google.com"
chrome-navigate.js --list
chrome-navigate.js --select 0
chrome-navigate.js --close 1
chrome-navigate.js --wait "Login successful"
chrome-navigate.js --resize 1920 1080
```

Navigate pages and manage browser tabs.

**Navigation:**
- `<url>`: Go to URL
- `--back`: History back
- `--forward`: History forward
- `--reload`: Reload (add `--no-cache` to bypass cache)
- `--wait <text>`: Wait for text to appear

**Page Management:**
- `--new <url>`: Open new tab
- `--list`: List open pages
- `--select <idx>`: Select page by index
- `--close <idx>`: Close page by index
- `--resize W H`: Set viewport size

## Eval (JavaScript)

```bash
chrome-eval.js '() => document.title'
chrome-eval.js '() => window.location.href'
chrome-eval.js '() => document.querySelectorAll("a").length'
chrome-eval.js 'async () => await fetch("/api").then(r => r.json())'
```

Execute JavaScript in page context. Must return JSON-serializable values.

**With element args:**
```bash
chrome-eval.js '(el) => el.innerText' --args '[{"uid":"heading"}]'
chrome-eval.js '(el) => el.getBoundingClientRect()' --args '[{"uid":"hero"}]'
```

## Console

```bash
chrome-console.js
chrome-console.js --types error,warn
chrome-console.js --preserved --limit 50
chrome-console.js --get 42
```

List or retrieve browser console messages.

**Options:**
- `--types LIST`: Filter (log, error, warn, info, debug, etc.)
- `--preserved`: Include last 3 navigations
- `--limit N`: Max messages
- `--get <id>`: Get specific message

## Network

```bash
chrome-network.js
chrome-network.js --types xhr,fetch
chrome-network.js --preserved --limit 100
chrome-network.js --get 123
chrome-network.js --get              # Get selected in DevTools
```

List or retrieve network requests.

**Options:**
- `--types LIST`: Filter (xhr, fetch, document, script, image, etc.)
- `--preserved`: Include last 3 navigations
- `--limit N`: Max requests
- `--get [id]`: Get request details (omit id for DevTools selection)

## Emulate

```bash
chrome-emulate.js --network "Slow 3G"
chrome-emulate.js --network "Offline"
chrome-emulate.js --network "No emulation"
chrome-emulate.js --cpu 4
chrome-emulate.js --geo 37.7749 -122.4194
chrome-emulate.js --geo-clear
```

Emulate device conditions.

**Network:** `Offline`, `Slow 3G`, `Fast 3G`, `Slow 4G`, `Fast 4G`, `No emulation`

**CPU:** Slowdown factor 1-20 (1 = no throttle)

**Geo:** Latitude (-90 to 90), Longitude (-180 to 180)

## Performance

```bash
chrome-perf.js --start --reload --auto-stop
chrome-perf.js --start --reload
chrome-perf.js --stop
chrome-perf.js --insight "set-123" "LCPBreakdown"
```

Performance tracing and Core Web Vitals.

**Options:**
- `--start`: Begin trace
  - `--reload`: Reload page when starting
  - `--auto-stop`: Auto-stop recording
- `--stop`: End trace
- `--insight <setId> <name>`: Analyze insight (DocumentLatency, LCPBreakdown, etc.)

## Split Image (for large screenshots)

```bash
chrome-split-image.js /tmp/full-page.png
chrome-split-image.js /tmp/full-page.png --max-height 5000
chrome-split-image.js /tmp/full-page.png --output /tmp/sections
chrome-split-image.js /tmp/full-page.png --info
```

Split large screenshots into sections that fit within API size limits (8000px).

**Options:**
- `--max-height N`: Max height per section (default: 7500px)
- `--output DIR`: Output directory (default: same as input)
- `--info`: Just show dimensions, don't split

**Output:** Creates `filename-1.png`, `filename-2.png`, etc. and lists them for easy viewing.

## Other Tools

```bash
chrome-drag.js "item" "drop-zone"     # Drag and drop
chrome-upload.js "input" "/path.pdf"  # File upload
chrome-dialog.js --accept             # Accept alert/confirm
chrome-dialog.js --accept "text"      # Accept prompt with text
chrome-dialog.js --dismiss            # Dismiss dialog
```

## Token Efficiency Best Practices

1. **Snapshot first**: Always run `chrome-snapshot.js` to get UIDs before interactions
2. **Batch operations**: Use `chrome-fill.js --form` for multiple fields
3. **Targeted screenshots**: Use `--uid` to capture only what you need
4. **Filter console/network**: Use `--types` to reduce output
5. **Efficient scrolling**: Use `chrome-scroll.js page-down` for quick navigation

## Example Workflow

```bash
# 1. Navigate to page
chrome-navigate.js "https://example.com/login"

# 2. Get element UIDs
chrome-snapshot.js

# 3. Fill login form
chrome-fill.js --form '[{"uid":"email","value":"user@example.com"},{"uid":"password","value":"secret"}]'

# 4. Click submit
chrome-click.js "submit-btn"

# 5. Wait for redirect
chrome-navigate.js --wait "Dashboard"

# 6. Take screenshot
chrome-screenshot.js --file /tmp/dashboard.png
```

## Troubleshooting

### "command not found" errors

```bash
# Check if tools are in PATH
which chrome-navigate.js

# If not found, add the directory to PATH
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/agent-tools/chrome-dev-control:$PATH"' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

### "image dimensions exceed max" error

Full-page screenshots can exceed Claude's 8000px limit. Split them into sections:

```bash
# Take full-page screenshot
chrome-screenshot.js --full --file /tmp/full-page.png

# Split into viewable sections
chrome-split-image.js /tmp/full-page.png

# Output: /tmp/full-page-1.png, /tmp/full-page-2.png, etc.
# Read each section to view the entire page
```

### Cannot connect to Chrome

Ensure Chrome is running with DevTools accessible. The tools use `@anthropic-ai/chrome-devtools-mcp` via mcporter.

### mcporter not installed

```bash
npm install -g mcporter
```
